title: break and continue
learningObjectives: Explain how break exits the nearest enclosing loop or switch.
Explain how continue skips the rest of the current loop iteration.
Distinguish the effect of break and continue in while, do-while and for loops.
Use control-transfer statements without bypassing required cleanup or state updates.
Trace nested loops to identify which construct a break or continue affects.

understand.concept: The break statement terminates the nearest enclosing iteration or switch statement. The continue statement skips the remainder of the current iteration and proceeds to the next loop cycle; in a for loop, the iteration expression runs before the next condition test. In nested loops, these statements affect only the nearest enclosing loop or switch as specified by the language.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding break and continue helps you reason about program behaviour instead of memorizing syntax. It is useful in exams, debugging and building reliable C applications.
understand.analogy: Treat the concept as a tool with a precise contract: it has valid inputs, defined operations and observable results.
understand.analogyLimit: An analogy is only an aid; the C standard and the relevant function specifications determine actual behaviour.

explain.narrative:
## 1. break

A break statement immediately exits the nearest enclosing while, do-while, for or switch statement. Execution continues after that construct. It is useful when a search finds its target or a menu selection requests exit.

## 2. continue

A continue statement skips the remaining statements in the current iteration. The loop then proceeds according to its kind: a for loop evaluates its iteration expression before checking the condition again; a while or do-while proceeds to its condition check.

## 3. Nested loops

Inside nested loops, break and continue affect the innermost enclosing loop. They do not automatically exit every surrounding loop. Use a clearly designed flag, helper function or other explicit structure when an outer loop must also stop.

## 4. Avoid skipped essential work

A continue placed before a required update in a while loop can accidentally prevent progress and create an infinite loop. Make sure resource cleanup and state updates are not bypassed.

## 5. Prefer clear control flow

Use break and continue when they simplify the loop. If many control transfers make the code difficult to follow, restructure the loop or extract a function.

questions.prompt: What does break do inside a loop?
questions.explanation: break terminates the nearest enclosing iteration or switch statement.

options: Skips the rest of the current iteration and proceeds to the next loop cycle
questions.answer: Skips the rest of the current iteration and proceeds to the next loop cycle
questions.explanation: continue does not terminate the loop.

questions.prompt: In a for loop, what happens after continue?
options: The iteration expression runs, then the condition is checked
questions.answer: The iteration expression runs, then the condition is checked
questions.explanation: The for-loop continuation sequence includes the iteration expression.

questions.prompt: In nested loops, which loop does break exit?
questions.explanation: break affects the innermost enclosing loop or switch.
